Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: final vertical wildlife photograph
Input image: Image 1 is the edit target.
Primary request: Change only the ground surface under and in front of the panther's paws, approximately the bottom third of the frame. Replace the generated-looking orange crumbly ground with a natural, geologically convincing sandstone ledge.
Materials/textures: fine horizontal bedding lines and subtle cross-bedding; a clean natural fracture edge; smooth wind-worn faces; sparse loose grit and only a few small pebbles; irregular dark desert-varnish streaks; natural colour variation from rust through muted orange to pale ochre.
Depth of field: preserve the look of a 400mm wildlife lens focused on the panther's eye. Only the narrow strip of sandstone directly under the paws is sharp; the nearest ground at the bottom of frame becomes softly and naturally out of focus.
Lighting: keep the existing torch lighting exactly; it rakes across the ledge so the far edge catches a warm glow while the near foreground falls into shadow.
Hard invariants: Preserve the panther pixel-faithfully—identity, anatomy, pose, paws, claws, fur, wetness, eye, whiskers and silhouette. Preserve all lighting on the panther, colour grade, airborne particles, background canyon, framing, camera angle, depth of field outside the edited ground, and composition exactly as in the source. Do not modify anything above the ground boundary. No added objects, animals, vegetation, text, logos, or watermark.
Avoid: repeated sponge-like lumps, uniform crumb texture, equally sharp texture across the foreground, flat saturated orange, even lighting, oversharpening, CGI or generated-looking surfaces.
